questions.question: On what exact date does the lease expire?
questions.why: The model is run for every year from 2030 to 2035 because the date is not known; the sale price as is differs by about a tenth between the earliest and latest year.
questions.have: Only the window in the brief: 2030 to 2035.
questions.how: Read the term clause, every amendment and any commencement-date memorandum. Check the Recorder's index for a recorded memorandum of lease.

questions.question: What is the rent today, and does it rise during the term?
questions.why: Every money figure on this site is per $100 of yearly rent until the rent is known. Whether rent rises is among the settings that move the answer most.
questions.have: The tenant says its leases are generally fixed rent with cost-of-living adjustments.
questions.how: Lease rent schedule and the last twelve months of rent receipts.

questions.question: Does the tenant hold renewal options: how many, at what rent, with what notice window?
questions.why: Options decide who controls the renewal and when the answer will be known. A missed notice window can settle the matter by default.
questions.have: The tenant says it has generally been able to renew its leases at then-current market rates.
questions.how: Lease option clause; put each notice date in a calendar.

questions.question: Who is the tenant: the company, a subsidiary or a franchisee, and is there a guaranty?
questions.why: The rent is only as good as the party that owes it. 93% of the system is franchised.
questions.have: How the system holds its sites: 164 company-owned, 565 company building on leased land, 1,020 leased by the company, 387 held directly by franchisees.
questions.how: Tenant name on the lease and any assignment; guaranty document; tenant estoppel certificate.

questions.question: Is the lease fully net: who pays taxes, insurance, roof, structure and parking lot?
questions.why: If roof and structure are the owner's, the income is not as net as assumed and a buyer will pay less.
questions.have: The tenant describes its leases as fixed rent plus real estate taxes, insurance and other expenses.
questions.how: Lease repair, maintenance, tax and insurance clauses; latest tax bill.

questions.question: What happens under the lease after a fire, earthquake or condemnation?
questions.why: This clause decides who bears a disaster: whether the tenant must rebuild, whether rent stops, and whether either side can walk away.
questions.have: The law lets a property be rebuilt after a declared disaster without a new assessed value, and lets the assessed value move to a replacement property in the county.
questions.how: Lease casualty, condemnation and insurance clauses, reviewed by a real-estate attorney.

questions.question: Can the tenant assign, sublet or stop operating, and does it have a right of first refusal or an option to buy?
questions.why: A right of first refusal changes how a sale must be run; a right to go dark changes what an extension is worth.
questions.have: Nothing.
questions.how: Lease assignment, operating and purchase-right clauses; title report for recorded rights.

questions.question: Is it a lease of the building or of the land only?
questions.why: In a ground lease the building may revert to the owner at expiry, which changes the value of the site without the tenant.
questions.have: The company owns 565 buildings on land it leases, so ground leases are common in its system.
questions.how: Premises clause and the clause on improvements at expiry.

questions.question: Will the tenant sign an early extension if asked now?
questions.why: In the model the answer splits the decision. After a refusal, selling beats keeping on both the typical and the bad outcome; after an agreement, keeping and selling are close on the typical outcome and differ on the bad one.
questions.have: The tenant is closing older, weaker restaurants and has an interim chief executive.
questions.how: Ask the tenant's real-estate department in writing for a proposal: term, rent, increases, options. Asking commits the owner to nothing.
questions.who: Owner, with a net-lease broker or attorney

questions.question: How is this restaurant trading: yearly sales and rent as a share of sales?
questions.why: A restaurant that trades well is renewed even when the system shrinks; one that trades badly is a closure candidate.
questions.have: System-wide same-store sales: -1.1% in the latest quarter, -4.2% in fiscal 2025.
questions.how: Ask the tenant for unit sales; check whether the lease entitles the owner to sales reports.

questions.question: Is this restaurant on a closure list or due a remodel, and when does its franchise agreement end?
questions.why: The company said the remaining closures follow franchise agreement termination dates, and that most targeted restaurants have been in the system for over three decades.
questions.have: Programme size and timing: approximately 150-200 restaurants; approximately 80-120 by 12/31/2025.
questions.how: Ask the tenant directly; check city building records for recent remodel permits.

questions.question: How strong is the tenant's credit today?
questions.why: A leveraged tenant can renew and still fail later.
questions.have: Answered from filings: stockholders' deficit, debt, earnings, cash flow and refinancing are on the Tenant page. The annual report for the fiscal year ended in late September 2026 was not yet filed on the access date.
questions.how: Re-read when the next Form 10-K is filed.

questions.question: What would the property sell for today as it stands, and with an extension signed?
questions.why: The gap between the two is the value of asking for an extension before selling; in the model it is 2% to 13% depending on the expiry year.
questions.have: Only national averages for long leases: purchase yields of 6.5% to 7.3%.
questions.how: Two broker opinions of value from net-lease brokers with closed Los Angeles restaurant sales, each stating its comparables; or a certified appraisal.

questions.question: What is the land worth if the tenant leaves?
questions.why: Land value is the floor under every hold strategy. In a national portfolio empty buildings sold for 63% of the leased price per square foot; scarce Los Angeles land may hold up better or the building may be a liability.
questions.have: A national ratio only.
questions.how: Ask the appraiser for a land-residual value; look up zoning and lot size privately.

questions.question: Is the likely price near $5,400,000?
questions.why: Above that price the city tax is 4% of the whole price, an extra $216,000 at the threshold.
questions.have: The rule and the threshold are verified.
questions.how: Compare the broker opinions with the threshold before deciding how to market.

questions.question: What is the owner's tax basis, and how much depreciation has been taken?
questions.why: It sets the tax on a cash sale, which can take a large share of the price, and so decides between a cash sale and an exchange.
questions.have: The statutory rates: 20% plus 3.8% federal, 25% on past depreciation, up to 13.30% in California.
questions.how: Tax returns and depreciation schedule, reviewed with a tax adviser. Keep the figures out of this repository.

questions.question: Is there a loan on the property, and what would it cost to repay early?
questions.why: A prepayment charge or a due-on-sale clause changes the proceeds and the timing.
questions.have: Nothing.
questions.how: Loan statement and note.

questions.question: What does the owner need from this asset: income, a time horizon, and how much loss is tolerable?
questions.why: 'Manageable risk' is the owner's to define. The model's ranking changes with the weight put on a bad outcome.
questions.have: Nothing; the base case weighs the typical and the bad outcome equally.
questions.how: A private conversation with the owner's financial adviser; record only the resulting constraints.

questions.question: What is the estate plan?
questions.why: Property held until death generally takes a new basis at market value, while a sale in life is taxed; heirs' property tax is reset either way.
questions.have: The rules are verified.
questions.how: Owner's estate attorney.

questions.question: How is title held, and who must agree to a sale or an extension?
questions.why: A trust or co-owners can add consents and time.
questions.have: Nothing.
questions.how: Vesting deed or preliminary title report.

questions.question: If the property is sold, would the owner exchange into another property, and of what kind?
questions.why: An exchange must name a replacement within 45 days and close within 180 days; the replacement's tenant and location decide whether risk actually falls.
questions.have: The exchange rules are verified.
questions.how: Agree criteria (tenant strength, lease length, region) and shortlist candidates before listing.

questions.question: Is the customer base around the property growing or shrinking?
questions.why: Fewer residents and households mean fewer visits over a ten-year renewal.
questions.have: Answered for city and county: residents are down since 2020 and the State projects a further small decline to 2035.
questions.how: With the address in hand privately, pull census-tract figures for one and three miles.

questions.question: Are local jobs and incomes supporting restaurant spending?
questions.why: Fast food depends on nearby workers and households with modest incomes.
questions.have: Answered for metro and county: unemployment 4.5%, payroll jobs up 0.5% over the year, restaurant jobs up 2.1%, median household income $81,939 in the city.
questions.how: County output figure from BEA's interactive tables.

questions.question: What is happening to schools and families nearby?
questions.why: School enrollment is the clearest official signal of families leaving.
questions.have: Answered for county and district: public enrollment fell 18.4% in ten years and is projected to fall a further 19.4% by 2035-36; Los Angeles Unified enrolls 497,105.
questions.how: With the address, list nearby schools and their enrollment trend from the State school directory.

questions.question: Is anything planned near the site: transit, public works, rezoning?
questions.why: Such changes can raise land value or restrict drive-through use.
questions.have: Nothing parcel-specific.
questions.how: City Planning zoning search and public counter.

questions.question: How do wage rules bear on this tenant?
questions.why: Labor is the cost the tenant controls least.
questions.have: Answered: $20.00 an hour for covered fast-food employers, above the city minimum of $18.42; a state council can raise it.
questions.how: Watch for council decisions.

questions.question: Is the parcel in a mapped fire, flood, fault, liquefaction or landslide zone?
questions.why: Regional odds say little about one site. The zones are free to look up but need the address.
questions.have: Regional record: 60% chance of a magnitude 6.7 or larger earthquake in 30 years from 2014; 16,264 structures destroyed in the January 2025 fires.
questions.how: Enter the address privately in the three official map tools linked in the rows.

questions.question: What is the building made of, when was it built, and is it under a retrofit order?
questions.why: Structure decides damage. The city requires retrofits of two older building types.
questions.have: The ordinance is verified.
questions.how: City building records; an engineer's walk-through if the building predates 1978.

questions.question: What insurance is in force, does it cover earthquake, and who pays?
questions.why: Earthquake damage is commonly excluded from standard property cover; the lease and the policy together decide the owner's loss.
questions.have: The insurance market is under strain: a $1 billion assessment was approved after the 2025 fires.
questions.how: Current policies and certificates from tenant and owner; a quote for earthquake cover.

questions.question: What is the federal risk index rating for the county?
questions.why: A second official view of hazard.
questions.have: Nothing: the official address returned an error on the access date.
questions.how: Re-open the National Risk Index county report.

questions.question: Will the city transfer tax or the state tax rates change before a sale?
questions.why: A 4% tax on the whole price is larger than a typical brokerage fee.
questions.have: Verified: thresholds rose on July 1, 2026; a measure to make higher state rates permanent leads 60.7% to 39.3% in the unofficial count; results become official by December 11, 2026.
questions.how: Re-check the Secretary of State's certified results and ask the transaction attorney about pending challenges to the city tax.

questions.question: Is there an environmental problem on or near the site?
questions.why: Cleanup liability can outlast a sale.
questions.have: Nothing: the address is withheld.
questions.how: Search the State's cleanup database privately; order a Phase I assessment.

questions.question: How much extra yield does a buyer demand for a short lease?
questions.why: It is a model setting that no official source measures.
questions.have: Only that filed purchase yields are for leases of about 19.6 years.
questions.how: Ask each broker to price the lease as is and as extended, in writing.
